Contract.title: The kernel refreshes installed skills only from committed skill text and pins LF for every text file
Contract.Problem: Explicit owner decision of 2026-11-16: the kernel must not install uncommitted skill text into a governed repository, and the repository must pin LF. Observed failure: the running checkout can be modified in exactly the files a refresh reads, and `git status` on those files is the only thing between them and every governed repository. Observed failure: without `.gitattributes`, a fresh clone with `core.autocrlf=true` checks out CRLF and `bun run package:verify` reports drift for every generated file, failing a release check on a platform rather than on a defect. Installed-skill drift remains outside the target contract.
Contract.Change: `grace5 upgrade` refuses before it prints the plan and before it writes anything when the chain contains a migration step and the running kernel checkout's `skills/` or `packages/skills/` differs from its `HEAD`; the refusal names each modified path and exits 1. A pin bump reads no skills and is not refused; a checkout without `.git` is not checked. `.gitattributes` pins `eol=lf` for text; the index is already LF and no blob is renormalised. The refusal is stated in the command help, `upgrade.md`, `commands.md` and a new conformance case; no installed skill byte, state layout, command, flag, schema or record changes.

Constraints.Constraint: The surface grows by nothing: no command, flag, schema, record kind, skill or validation mechanism is added; the change is the guard, `.gitattributes`, its tests and the documents that state it.
An ordinary change does not bump the version, the pin or a tag and registers no migration boundary or row; this change does none of those and adds no release.
Installed `grace5-*` skills stay kernel-managed and the guard writes nothing, so no candidate, dirty state, diff or evidence changes.
The guard is a kernel mechanism and adds one ledger entry with its removal criterion; `.gitattributes` is repository configuration, not a kernel mechanism, and adds none.
`skills/`, `packages/`, `package.json` and `.grace5/kernel-version` are Protected: the guard must not change installed bytes, generated packages, the version surfaces or the pin.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No deletion or consolidation of the skill copies: `packages/` and `skills/` stay as they are; the one-copy or single-channel design waits for the installation process.
No drift detection or repair for installed skills, in `status` or `upgrade`; drift stays outside the target contract.
No installer, seeding, skill-location change or new skill; installation remains separate from the kernel.
No tag or commit-ancestry enforcement: a clean but untagged checkout is still accepted; only a dirty skill source is refused.
No change to `run`, `check`, `close`, `status` or the refresh semantics of a step.

Acceptance.Criterion: With a chain that contains a step, a kernel checkout whose `skills/` or `packages/skills/` differs from `HEAD` is refused before the plan is printed and before anything is written, with and without `--plan`, naming each modified path and exiting 1; the target repository's pin and installed skills are unchanged. A clean kernel source upgrades normally.
A chain of pin bumps only neither reads nor refuses a modified skill source, and no installed skill byte, generated package, candidate or evidence changes.
`eol=lf` applies to the canonical and packaged skill trees, and the index has no CRLF blob.
The command help and generated CLI reference carry the refusal, and `package:verify` still passes.

Trace.Expect: kernel skills are modified relative to HEAD

Decisions.Decision: The guard covers both the canonical `skills/` tree, which authors edit, and the `packages/skills/` tree the refresh reads; either being dirty refuses, and the line names the paths.
The guard runs only when the chain contains a migration step, because only a step refreshes skills and a pin bump reads none.
The refusal precedes the plan and every write, `--plan` included, so a plan cannot describe a refresh the kernel would not perform.
A kernel checkout without `.git` is not checked; a clean but untagged checkout is accepted. Closing that residual with a tag check is out of scope.
Installed-skill drift is not detected or repaired; this change protects the kernel source, not a governed repository's installed copies.
`.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf`; the index is already LF on all 231 tracked files, so the change renormalises no blob and alters no record.
